Bachelet, de 74 anos, anunciou sua decisão em um vídeo publicado no Instagram, dizendo: “Vou agora continuar, com a mesma determinação de sempre, meu trabalho internacional”. A duas vezes presidente do Chile e ex-chefe de direitos humanos da ONU havia baseado sua campanha na defesa do multilateralismo e do direito internacional, em um momento em que, segundo ela, ambos estão sob pressão constante. A desistência de Bachelet deixa sete candidatos na disputa para suceder o secretário-geral António Guterres, que concluirá seu segundo mandato de cinco anos em 31 de dezembro de 2026. Ainda é possível que mais candidatos entrem na disputa. Sua desistência ocorre apenas um dia depois que uma terceira sondagem informal, realizada na sexta-feira, mostrou que seu apoio havia praticamente desmoronado. A mesma sondagem colocou Rebeca Grynspan, da Costa Rica, na liderança. O Conselho de Segurança da ONU acabará por recomendar formalmente um único candidato à Assembleia Geral, composta por 193 membros, para a eleição. A aprovação da Assembleia é há muito vista como uma formalidade, uma vez que o Conselho chegue a um consenso.

item.title: Fed's Kashkari says inflation is still too high in 'all aspects' of US economy, in Fox News interview
item.description: Minneapolis Federal Reserve President Neel Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is too high across all sectors of the US economy, not just in rising oil prices.
item.dc:creator: Doina Chiacu
item.content:encoded: Minneapolis Federal Reserve President Neel Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is too high across all sectors of the US economy, not just in rising oil prices. "So even if we strip out energy, which is really volatile, and strip out food — they matter a lot — but in terms of where the economy is going, inflation is still too high," Kashkari told Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures." Kashkari supported the unanimous vote last week to raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point to 3.75%-4.00%. He was one of three officials to dissent at the Fed's prior meeting in favor of a hike when the majority of the Federal Open Market Committee then opted to leave rates unchanged. Projections released along with the rate-hike decision showed all but two Fed policymakers see at least one more quarter-point increase this year. Rate futures markets reflect a two-in-three chance that the Fed's policy rate ends 2026 in the 4.00% to 4.25% range, with a strong likelihood of it climbing by at least another quarter point beyond that by mid-2027. MIDDLE EAST CONFLICT DRIVES OIL SURGE Crude oil prices soared after hostilities intensified with the US and Iran attacking and sinking some oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz and Saudi Arabia closing its vital East-West pipeline due to aerial attacks in the widening Middle East war. The Fed's job is to get inflation back down to the central bank's 2% target, he said, and there is nothing it can do with interest rates that might result in opening up the Strait of Hormuz or bringing down oil prices. "The inflation that the American people are feeling every day is much beyond just oil prices. It's in all aspects of the economy. It's in the services sector, for example, widely. So we have tools to bring that back down," Kashkari said. "Hopefully, we'll get some help from other parts of government or other parts of the real economy." FED CHAIRMAN ECHOES INFLATION CONCERNS Kashkari's inflation concerns largely echoed those voiced by Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh after the conclusion of the latest rate-setting meeting on Wednesday. Warsh estimated that inflation as measured by the gauge the Fed uses to set its 2% target was likely around 3.6% in August, though that figure will not be released officially until later this month. "Too many categories are still posting increases above 3 percent, on both a six- and 12-month basis," Warsh said at his press conference following the meeting. Kashkari also said economic growth has been quite strong, even with the tariff and trade war and the conflicts in Ukraine and Iran. "The American economy has been very resilient." "Despite that, the US economy has been growing at a good clip, and productivity is showing some signs of improving. And so my hope is, as some of those conflicts go to the background, that the growth can really take over and hopefully bring inflation down. Hopefully, disinflation can take over, which will make the Fed's job a lot easier."

item.title: Red Sox eager to regain mojo in rubber match vs. 'relentless' Rays
item.description: Jahmai Jones said he feels the Boston Red Sox have grown this week, and perhaps he has a point.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jahmai Jones said he feels the Boston Red Sox have grown this week, and perhaps he has a point. After Trevor Story's late homer led Boston to a win in the finale of its previous series, the Red Sox will look to capture the decisive contest of their current set on Sunday against the Tampa Bay Rays in St. Petersburg, Fla. Jones homered from the designated hitter position in Friday's 4-2 victory over the Rays. He said the two games more resembled the way Boston has played during the second half of 2026. "We've had some big performances. I feel like it's a different guy every night," said Jones, who notched his sixth homer of the season in a night in which Roman Anthony went deep and had three RBIs. "Everybody in here knows what we're playing for. I feel we've had a lot of tight ball games. That last one in Texas (on Thursday) and then (Friday showed) who we are and what our baseball is." The Red Sox (84-71) saw their momentum slowed on Saturday, however, with a 2-1 setback to the Rays (94-60). They enter the game comfortably in line for the second wild card in the American League. Richie Palacios had an RBI single in the ninth inning to score Junior Caminero with the winning run. It marked the third walk-off win of the season-ending homestand for Tampa Bay. "We're just relentless. No matter what's going on in the game, we always feel like we have a chance to win," Palacios said. "Three walk-offs is amazing, and we're just going to continue to do what we do." Tampa Bay has won seven of its past eight games overall to move five games ahead of the second-place New York Yankees in the American League East. The teams each have eight games remaining on their schedule -- four of them against each other. The teams open their series Tuesday in New York with a doubleheader. "It's very encouraging. It's a good feeling," Rays manager Kevin Cash said following Saturday's game. "You want to get as many reps at that as possible, because we know the games that we're going to continue playing this year are going to be against good teams and in tight ballgames." Tampa Bay right-hander Griffin Jax (7-10, 3.80 ERA) is scheduled to start on Sunday. Jax scattered two hits over five scoreless innings and struck out seven in five innings of a no-decision against the Athletics last Tuesday. The Rays won 2-1. He is 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA in two starts against Boston this season. He is 0-2 with a 7.86 ERA in 16 career appearances (three starts) against the Red Sox. Boston left-hander Patrick Sandoval (1-6, 4.99) is the scheduled starter on Sunday. He has lost his past six decisions heading into Sunday's game, most recently a 4-2 setback to the Texas Rangers on Tuesday. He yielded four runs on four hits in 2 2/3 innings and threw 68 pitches. Sandoval is 0-3 with a 3.67 ERA in nine games (eight starts) against the Rays. The Red Sox would love to welcome back Ceddanne Rafaela, who suffered a right quadriceps strain on Sept. 2 in a game against the Seattle Mariners and was placed on the 10-day injured list. He was hitting .282 with 16 home runs, 32 doubles and 70 RBIs to go along with 17 stolen bases. --Field Level Media

item.title: Qatar launches wealth fund division for domestic investments
item.description: Qatar's prime minister announced on Sunday the creation of a new division of the Qatar Investment Authority dedicated to developing domestic investments, marking a new direction for a sovereign wealth fund long focused on building wealth overseas.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Mills
item.content:encoded: Qatar's prime minister announced on Sunday the creation of a new division of the Qatar Investment Authority dedicated to developing domestic investments, marking a new direction for a sovereign wealth fund long focused on building wealth overseas. The Gulf Arab state is facing financial strain due to the US-Israeli war on Iran and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, which has made it impossible for it to reliably export liquefied natural gas - still Qatar's primary income source despite efforts to diversify the economy. "We aim to expand the role of the private sector in driving Qatar's economic growth," Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani said as he announced the new division, Doha Investment, at a special edition of the Qatar Economic Forum in New York. The annual gathering was cancelled in May, following weeks of Iranian missile and drone attacks on Gulf states, including Qatar. "It will support our strongest companies, help emerging businesses grow, deepen capital markets and attract international capital and expertise to contribute to this effort," he added. DEDICATED MANAGER The new division will operate as the dedicated manager of QIA's local portfolio, initially overseeing 45 state-owned enterprises that represent roughly one-third of the wealth fund's total assets, according to Sheikh Faisal bin Thani Al Thani, Qatar's minister of commerce and industry. He will serve as managing director and vice-chairman of Doha Investment. Sheikh Faisal described the division not as a new creation but a consolidation, adding that the step has been under consideration for more than a decade. The QIA, which does not release comprehensive data on its holdings but is estimated by the research firm Global SWF to have assets under management of $580 billion, was established in 2005 with an original charter centred on deploying capital abroad. It has built up a domestic footprint in recent years, scaling up companies that have become national leaders, including Qatar Airways, lender QNB and telecoms company Ooredoo, developer Qatari Diar and hotels owner Katara Hospitality. The new division's mandate also spans strengthening and building new national champions, supporting privatisation, widening private-sector participation and diversifying Qatar's economy, Sheikh Faisal said. Qatar's non-hydrocarbon economy grew 4.8% in 2025, outpacing 2.9% overall real GDP growth, while non-hydrocarbon activities accounted for 65.5% of real GDP in the third quarter of this year, according to the Qatar Central Bank and National Planning Council.

item.title: D-backs strive to make more 'magic' happen vs. Yankees
item.description: Arizona manager Torey Lovullo said he felt "a little bit of magic" in a 5-3 walk-off win over the New York Yankees on Saturday, the night the Diamondbacks celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series title.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Arizona manager Torey Lovullo said he felt "a little bit of magic" in a 5-3 walk-off win over the New York Yankees on Saturday, the night the Diamondbacks celebrated the 25th anniversary of their 2001 World Series title. The Diamondbacks will take wins however they can get them as they continue an uphill fight for a National League wild-card berth in Sunday afternoon's finale of a three-game series vs. the Yankees in Phoenix. New York's Will Warren (10-6, 3.89 ERA) will oppose Arizona's Corbin Burnes (0-0, 5.87) in a battle of right-handers. "There was a ton of energy in the stadium," said Lovullo, noting that most of the players from the 2001 team were on hand, "so maybe there was a little bit of magic somewhere in these rafters that everybody picked up on." Pavin Smith's two-run, game-winning homer saved the Diamondbacks for a night, but work remains. "We have to get inside a certain number," said Lovullo, whose team will finish the regular season next week with a pair of three-game series at Colorado and San Diego. "We know it, and this team is driving for something they feel they are able to do." Arizona (81-74) is five games behind the Chicago Cubs (86-69) and San Diego (86-69) and four behind Philadelphia (85-70) for the NL's three wild-card spots. Each team has seven games remaining. The Yankees (89-65) fell five games behind first-place Tampa Bay (94-60) in the AL East. Those teams will meet in a four-game series in Yankee Stadium beginning with a split doubleheader on Tuesday and already have clinched a postseason berth. "I have a ton of confidence in the guys we have rolling out there right now," New York manager Aaron Boone said after Aaron Judge (calf strain) landed on the 10-day injured list Saturday. Warren worked the Yankees' playoff clincher Monday at Minnesota, although he did not get a decision after giving up two runs (both unearned) in 5 2/3 innings of an 8-3 win. He struck out six and walked two. Warren has been a workhorse on a staff that has faced injury issues. He will make his 29th start, second on the team behind Cam Schlittler (32). "We've got a veteran core that's been here before, and we're looking to do big things," Warren said of the upcoming postseason. Warren has faced the Diamondbacks once in his career, giving up two runs on one hit -- a Corbin Carroll two-run homer -- in five innings of a no-decision on April 1, 2025. Burnes will make his third start since being activated from the injured list Sept. 8 after a 15-month absence following Tommy John surgery. He gave up five runs in 4 2/3 innings but didn't figure into the decision in Monday's 8-7 victory over Miami, striking out four with no walks. "It's all about cutter command," Burnes said of his pet pitch, which he traditionally throws about 50% of the time. "Just have to be more consistent with that," Burnes is 0-2 with a 1.93 ERA in four career starts against the Yankees. Paul Goldschmidt is 10-for-34 with a homer against the four-time All-Star and 2021 NL Cy Young Award winner. --Field Level Media

item.title: Angels, Twins playing out disappointing seasons
item.description: The Los Angeles Angels head into the home finale of their 2026 season with a chance to do something they haven't accomplished since late June -- win back-to-back home series.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Los Angeles Angels head into the home finale of their 2026 season with a chance to do something they haven't accomplished since late June -- win back-to-back home series. The Angels (60-95), who played spoiler and took two of three games from the Seattle Mariners earlier in the week, will try for their third win in a four-game series against the Minnesota Twins (72-83) on Sunday afternoon in Anaheim, Calif. The last time Los Angeles took consecutive home series came June 22-28, winning two of three games from both the Baltimore Orioles and the Athletics. Kurt Suzuki's squad will finish the season with games against the A's on Tuesday and Wednesday in West Sacramento, Calif., and a four-game series at Seattle. The Angels need to go at least 3-4 to avoid losing 100 games in a season for the first time in franchise history. Rookie right-hander Ryan Johnson (5-8, 4.88 ERA), the Angels' second-round pick in the 2024 MLB Draft out of Dallas Baptist, entered August with a 2-6 record and a 7.63 ERA. But in eight starts since, he has mixed his cutter with sweepers and sinkers and a funky delivery to go 3-2 with a 2.03 ERA in eight starts, allowing just 29 hits in 44 1/3 innings with 33 strikeouts. He will be opposed by right-hander Dean Kremer (3-5, 5.35). Johnson comes in off a 2-1 victory over Seattle on Tuesday night when he allowed one run on six hits in six innings with a season-high seven strikeouts. He began the game by throwing 16 consecutive strikes, and threw first-pitch strikes to 18 of the 25 batters he faced. "That might be the best game he pitched this year, honestly," Angels manager Kurt Suzuki said. "What was it, (16) straight to start the game going for strikes? I thought he did a great job of mixing and matching, and he really attacked the strike zone." Johnson is 0-0 with a 3.86 ERA in two career appearances (one start) against the Twins. That start came on July 11 in Minneapolis when he allowed three runs on three hits, including a two-run homer by Royce Lewis, in five innings in a game Minnesota eventually won, 5-3. He did not figure into the decision. Kremer is 3-0 with a 2.18 ERA in four career starts against Los Angeles, including 1-0 with a 1.80 ERA in two starts at Angel Stadium. Minnesota will head to San Francisco for three games starting Monday, then finish the season at home with a three-game set against American League West leader Texas. The Twins are just 2-5 in their past seven games and have been walked off twice in three games by the Angels. The Twins led 5-2 heading into the bottom of the eighth on Saturday and eventually lost, 6-5, in 11 innings on a two-out, bases-loaded comebacker by Christian Moore that caromed off the leg of pitcher Taylor Rogers. "Unfortunately, we get the ground ball and it hits off his leg there," Minnesota manager Derek Shelton said. "(But) the story of the game is we didn't capitalize on our opportunities." The Twins finished 3-for-18 with runners in scoring position and left nine men on base. --Field Level Media

item.title: Mariners wrap up road schedule with rubber match vs. Rockies
item.description: The road hasn't been kind to the Seattle Mariners this year, but they could finish their three-game series against the Colorado Rockies in Denver on a positive note Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The road hasn't been kind to the Seattle Mariners this year, but they could finish their three-game series against the Colorado Rockies in Denver on a positive note Sunday afternoon. After Saturday night's 5-3 loss, Seattle (72-83) is limping to the finish line. The Mariners, who are 32-48 on the road, will send rookie left-hander Kade Anderson (1-2, 5.33 ERA) to the mound against Colorado right-hander Tomoyuki Sugano (12-10, 5.49) on Sunday. Anderson, who will face the Rockies for the first time in his career, made his major league debut with 5 2/3 solid innings against the Chicago Cubs on Aug. 22. He allowed five runs on seven hits over 4 1/3 innings in a 6-4 loss to the Los Angeles Angels last Monday. The Mariners are seven games out of the final American League wild-card spot with seven remaining and could be eliminated on Sunday. The fall from nearly reaching the 2025 World Series to sitting out this October is frustrating for the Mariners, who will end their season at home against Houston and the Angels after Sunday's game. "There's a lot of disappointment when you have really high expectations," right-hander Logan Gilbert said. "Just the timing of it, careers go really fast. People know that time flies. ... You only have situations like this so often, that you feel like you have really good players on a really good team and a division that's wide open. "These situations are rare, and you always want to take advantage of it when you can. We had high expectations, and this year just hasn't gone the way it could have -- and that's the most frustrating part." Frustration is an apt description for Colorado (57-98), which is on pace to lose 100 games for the fourth consecutive season. The New York Mets were the most recent team to lose 100 or more games in four straight years -- during their first four seasons of existence (1962-65). The Rockies have shown improvement -- they topped last season's win total before August -- but they have work to do before they can be a contender. They will likely finish with the worst team ERA in the majors for the fifth straight season. Sugano helped improve that stat through July 31, compiling a 4.47 ERA to go with an 11-4 record, but his season has soured. He is 1-6 since, and his ERA has risen to 5.49 in his last eight starts. Sugano is 0-2 with a 7.41 ERA in three September starts, and in his last two outings he has a 9.00 ERA, but he has a chance to bounce back against the Mariners. He faced them twice while with Baltimore last season, going 2-0 with a 1.46 ERA. Despite the recent struggles, Rockies manager Warren Schaeffer said he believes in Sugano. "He knows what he is doing -- his game planning, all of this stuff combined. In the big spots, he doesn't waver," Schaeffer said. "There's a confidence and a belief in himself. He just knows how to limit damage in big spots." --Field Level Media

item.title: Russian exiles cast votes to voice dissent to Putin and Ukraine war
item.description: Many described it as a moral duty, if a futile act of protest against Putin and the war.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russians living abroad cast their votes on Sunday, the final day of a [USN:L6N45B05C TEXT:"parliamentary election"], in what many described as a moral duty, if ultimately a futile act of protest against President Vladimir Putin and the war in Ukraine. One exiled Muscovite, who gave her name as Olga, waiting in line to vote in the Armenian capital Yerevan, said she had no expectation her ballot would change anything inside Russia. "It's about putting on a bit of a show," she said. "This is really more about symbolism, about bringing something positive, about solidarity." The State Duma election, the first since Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, is likely to be presented by the Kremlin as evidence of public support for Putin's policies and for a war that is now in its fifth year with no end in sight. Most anti-war candidates were barred from the ballot and the other major parties have consistently voted in line with the ruling United Russia on major issues. Hundreds of thousands of Russians, many of them young and well-educated, fled the country after the start of the war in Ukraine, settling in ex-Soviet countries like Georgia, Armenia and Kazakhstan, as well as across Europe and beyond. After years outside their home country, several Russians who spoke to Reuters said they remained determined to see change come to Russia. "We still have our whole lives ahead of us, and we really want to be in Russia one day and help build a new, democratic country," said 24-year-old Varvara from Moscow, who spoke to Reuters in Berlin. Some protesters outside the Russian embassy in the German capital held up a placard reading, in Russian, "Putin is a murderer and a war criminal", and signs in support of Russian prisoners jailed for speaking out against the war. Many voters expressed deep pessimism about Russia's future, even if the conflict ends soon. Others, including a man who gave his name as Valery, clung to the belief that casting a ballot still mattered. "I want to believe, with every fibre of my being, that we can still make a difference and vote against the ruling authorities," he told Reuters in Yerevan.

item.title: Fleming puts England identity at heart of test rebuild
item.description: England's new test coach Stephen Fleming said restoring the team's identity and standards would be as important as improving results, after a turbulent year for English cricket that brought renewed scrutiny of player behaviour and team culture.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: England's new test coach Stephen Fleming said restoring the team's identity and standards would be as important as improving results, after a turbulent year for English cricket that brought renewed scrutiny of player behaviour and team culture. Fleming was [USN:L1N43W0FU TEXT:"appointed in July"] following England's slide in results and a series of off-field incidents that led to Brendon McCullum's departure from the test role, amid accusations of a drinking culture amongst the players. The latest incident involved pace bowler [USN:L1N44L0L6 TEXT:"Brydon Carse"], who was handcuffed outside a nightclub following Durham's County Championship title-winning victory over Derbyshire, shortly after Joe Root had lifted a team midnight curfew. Fleming said work has already begun on shaping the team's identity after months of questions over the culture surrounding the England setup. "I would love to be in charge of the number one Test team in the world. That would be my aspiration," Fleming told reporters in Manchester. "But there's a piece of work there that's already begun and that's around our identity. There's been a lot of coverage around that and I think the way that players represent England and the group is going to be really important to me. "The style of play will come with that also and that'll be a little bit more player-directed, but I feel very strongly about finding a sense of belonging within the group." Fleming said steps had already been taken behind the scenes, although he did not provide further details. “We've done some things to start that piece of work, so that's really important to me," Fleming said. "So not only will we be in the best position to win cricket games but also represent the England cricket team in its best form." Marcus Trescothick guided England to a 3-0 sweep of Pakistan as interim coach in August and September, before handing over to Fleming for December and January's three-test tour of South Africa. McCullum remains coach of England's white-ball sides. England begin a three-match one-day international series against Sri Lanka on Tuesday.

item.title: Trump convertirá el arco del triunfo en un complejo militar
item.description: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el domingo que había accedido a una petición de las Fuerzas Armadas para convertir el arco del triunfo que había propuesto construir cerca del Cementerio Nacional de Arlington, en Washington, en un complejo destinado a albergar y desplegar drones y munición para francotiradores.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el domingo que había accedido a una petición de las Fuerzas Armadas para convertir el arco del triunfo que había propuesto construir cerca del Cementerio Nacional de Arlington, en Washington, en un complejo destinado a albergar y desplegar drones y munición para francotiradores. El presidente alegó motivos de seguridad nacional para justificar la medida, sin mencionar ninguna amenaza concreta. El proyecto es parte de una iniciativa más amplia del presidente para remodelar el paisaje monumental de Washington, que incluye un nuevo salón de baile en la Casa Blanca, la renovación del estanque reflectante del Monumento a Lincoln y la remodelación de un campo de golf en el Parque East Potomac. En una publicación en las redes sociales, Trump dijo que, a "petición expresa" de las Fuerzas Armadas, había accedido a convertir el arco de 76 metros "en un complejo militar de primer orden y un arco del triunfo, para albergar, almacenar y disponer de la capacidad de utilizar rápidamente un gran número de drones, además de francotiradores, tanto en la azotea como en la plaza, y, además, almacenar grandes cantidades de munición para francotiradores". La Casa Blanca y el Departamento de Defensa no respondieron de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios. La Administración Federal de Aviación dijo la semana pasada que el arco, de 76 metros de altura, no supondría un peligro para las aeronaves, pero que sería necesario que contara con una "llama eterna" en su parte superior, lo que despeja un obstáculo aeronáutico para el monumento, que Trump propuso para conmemorar el aniversario 250 del país. Los expertos en aviación han expresado su preocupación por la seguridad, dada su proximidad al Aeropuerto Nacional Reagan de Washington, mientras que veteranos han presentado una demanda para impedir la construcción del arco, argumentando que destruiría la histórica línea de visión entre el Monumento a Lincoln y el Cementerio Nacional de Arlington.

item.title: Cardinals bid farewell to Nationals, Busch Stadium for 2026
item.description: The visiting Washington Nationals will look to complete a three-game sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The visiting Washington Nationals will look to complete a three-game sweep of the St. Louis Cardinals on Sunday afternoon. It will be the final home game of the season for the Cardinals, who are 37-43 at Busch Stadium. On Saturday, the Nationals scored four runs in the top of the 11th inning and held on for an 8-5 win. Washington (73-82) has won six of its past seven games, and a victory Sunday would give the team a .500 mark in September (8-8) despite a recent seven-game losing streak. The Cardinals (75-80), meanwhile, have lost four games in a row. After Sunday's game, they will finish the season at Pittsburgh and Milwaukee. Both St. Louis and Washington sit fourth in their respective divisions with seven games remaining, and both have been eliminated from postseason contention. The Nationals will start right-hander Jake Irvin (2-9, 5.51 ERA) on Sunday, and the Cardinals will counter with rookie left-hander Quinn Mathews (2-3, 3.62). Irvin has struggled since returning from the injured list in late July, going 0-5 with a 5.84 ERA in nine games (eight starts). Last time out, he followed an opener for the first time in his four-year career and gave up three runs on two hits and four walks over five innings against the Los Angeles Angels on Sept. 12. He struck out six and didn't figure into the decision of a 6-5 loss in 10 innings. Irvin has allowed 16 first-inning runs in 19 starts this season. Mathews will make his eighth major league start. Over his past four starts, he is 2-1 with a 1.93 ERA. In his most recent game, he allowed one run on four hits over 6 2/3 innings of a 2-1 win Monday against the San Francisco Giants. He struck out a career-high eight batters and walked two. He retired the first 10 batters he faced and did not allow a hit until the sixth. "(Catcher Leo Bernal) kind of navigated the first three innings -- I think I shook one pitch in three innings, which is unbelievable, to be honest with you," Mathews said. "So a lot of credit to Bernal there, getting me through the first three when I wasn't as sharp as I would have liked to have been." Saturday night, the Nationals won despite blowing their 40th and 41st save chances of the season, losing a 3-2 lead in the ninth and a 4-3 lead in the 10th. Jose Tena had the big hit in the 11th, a two-run double, and the bullpen held on, with Will Dion getting the final out for his first major league save. Washington's Jorbit Vivas had four hits, and Daylen Lile smacked a two-run homer. Jose Fermin and Ivan Herrera had three hits each for St. Louis. The Cardinals pulled to 8-5 and loaded the bases with no outs in the bottom of the 11th, but Nationals relievers retired three hitters in a row -- two by strikeout -- to end the game. For the game, St. Louis was called for a catcher's interference, committed two errors and left 13 men on base. "They've done a really nice job of playing some pretty clean baseball," manager Oliver Marmol said of his team, "and even when we don't, you have the winning run up to the plate in extra innings. There's parts of that game that are highly frustrating." --Field Level Media

item.title: Rangers look for length from Jacob deGrom in finale vs. Jays
item.description: The Texas Rangers have had to turn to their bullpen more often than they would have liked in the first two contests of their three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays in Arlington, Texas.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Texas Rangers have had to turn to their bullpen more often than they would have liked in the first two contests of their three-game series against the Toronto Blue Jays in Arlington, Texas. After pulling starter Kumar Rocker in the fifth inning of Friday's 7-1 win, Texas manager Skip Schumaker was forced to go to his bullpen with one out in the second on Saturday after starter Cal Quantrill exited the game with right lat tightness. Jordan Montgomery stepped in and held Toronto hitless over 3 2/3 innings in a 6-2 victory. Schumaker hopes to give his relievers a breather when Jacob deGrom takes the mound in the finale against the Blue Jays on Sunday afternoon. "That's what this team is all about right now," Schumaker said. "... Monty was fantastic. But again, these are team wins, and it's also because of what happened the day before, really covering us today." The veteran deGrom (11-9, 3.79 ERA) has been strong at home this season. The right-hander has a 2.53 ERA with 111 strikeouts in 85 1/3 innings over 15 starts at Globe Life Field. He's coming off an outing in which he allowed just two runs on three hits in five innings against the Boston Red Sox on Sept. 15. He has only made three starts against the Blue Jays in his career, going 1-1 with a 1.65 ERA. The Rangers (78-77) are eyeing a third straight win and a seventh in eight games. Saturday's victory combined with the Houston Astros' loss to the Atlanta Braves, propelled Texas into sole possession of first place in the American League West. "We're just here showing up every day to play and try and get in the playoffs," outfielder Wyatt Langford said. "To be in that position right now is great. But yeah, there are still a lot of games left. We need to keep it that way." While the playoff picture is looking up for Texas, the hopes continue to fade for Toronto (76-79), which has dropped four of its past five. The loss dropped the Blue Jays to three games behind the final wild card in the AL, currently held by the Chicago White Sox, with seven games remaining in the season. Toronto trailed 3-0 after two innings. The Blue Jays didn't get their first baserunner until Vladimir Guerrero Jr. walked in the fourth inning, and didn't get their first hit until the sixth. But pitching struggles in the bottom of the sixth allowed the Rangers to tack on three more runs. "It feels like the last couple games you're down early, and it makes it a little bit tougher to come back," manager John Schneider said. "You're looking for a big swing, a three-run homer or a base hit to score a couple to get back into it. I think falling behind early makes it a little bit tougher." Spencer Miles (6-2, 2.65) will get the start in what is expected to be a bullpen game for Toronto on Sunday. It'll be the second career appearance against Texas for the 26-year-old righty, who gave up just one hit in 2 2/3 innings of a relief appearance in a no-decision versus the Rangers on June 26. --Field Level Media

item.title: Irán advierte de una nueva escalada de Estados Unidos y sus aliados
item.description: Irán advirtió el domingo contra cualquier nuevo ataque de gran envergadura de Estados Unidos y sus aliados, y dijo que disponía de información según la cual se estaba preparando una acción de este tipo, lo que aumentó la inquietud en una región ya sacudida por los ataques con drones y misiles contra Arabia Saudita .
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir
item.content:encoded: Irán advirtió el domingo contra cualquier nuevo ataque de gran envergadura de Estados Unidos y sus aliados, y dijo que disponía de información según la cual se estaba preparando una acción de este tipo, lo que aumentó la inquietud en una región ya sacudida por los ataques con drones y misiles contra Arabia Saudita . El mando central militar de Irán dijo en medios de comunicación estatales que cualquier nuevo ataque desencadenaría una represalia sostenida contra las bases y los intereses estadounidenses, y que los aliados regionales de Washington serían considerados partes en el conflicto. No dio más detalles sobre la información de la que, dijo, disponía acerca de un inminente ataque estadounidense. El Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos emitió el sábado una alerta de seguridad en la que indicaba que existía la posibilidad de una escalada imprevista en Oriente Medio y que los estadounidenses debían redoblar la vigilancia y estar atentos a posibles cancelaciones de vuelos y cierres del espacio aéreo. A punto de cumplirse siete meses de la guerra entre Estados Unidos e Irán, ninguna de las partes parece dispuesta a hacer concesiones importantes para poner fin a los combates y, con los mercados energéticos mundiales ya al límite, el conflicto sigue extendiéndose en la región. El sábado, los hutíes de Yemen, respaldados por Irán, dijeron haber llevado a cabo ataques en la capital saudita, Riad, y contra una importante instalación petrolera en el puerto de Yanbu, en el mar Rojo. Arabia Saudita no hizo comentarios sobre el incidente ni sobre las afirmaciones de los hutíes. La alerta del Departamento de Estado de Estados Unidos mencionaba las hostilidades de los hutíes contra Arabia Saudita, incluidos los aeropuertos civiles. La reciente escalada de los hutíes ha obligado a Riad a enfrentarse a un doloroso dilema: continuar con los ataques aéreos contra el grupo para impedir que se apodere de más territorio yemení o dar un paso atrás con la esperanza de evitar ataques con drones contra infraestructuras críticas. Los avances de los hutíes a lo largo de la costa significan que las fuerzas del grupo se sitúan ahora en el estrecho de Mandeb, lo que les facilita el control del tráfico marítimo entre el mar Rojo y Asia y les permite bloquear esta vía navegable crucial. Dado que Irán ya ha bloqueado la mayor parte del tráfico marítimo en el estrecho de Ormuz, las exportaciones energéticas del golfo Pérsico, rico en petróleo, están ahora casi totalmente aisladas de los mercados mundiales, lo que aumenta la presión sobre los precios mundiales del petróleo. Por su parte, el bloqueo estadounidense de los puertos iraníes impide a Irán vender su propio petróleo, lo que contribuye a los graves problemas de la economía de la República Islámica. Irán reiteró el domingo que no reabriría el estrecho de Ormuz hasta que se cumplan los términos de un acuerdo de junio, tal y como los interpretaba. El presidente del Parlamento iraní, Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, dijo que Irán tendría que seguir luchando, además de negociando, para hacer retroceder a sus enemigos y consolidar cualquier avance logrado mediante la diplomacia.

item.title: Ronald Acuna Jr., Braves bid to clinch NL East in finale vs. Astros
item.description: Atlanta Braves right fielder Ronald Acuna Jr. rode a torrid 20-game stretch into the middle contest Saturday of an interleague series against the Houston Astros, and he continued his stellar play.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Atlanta Braves right fielder Ronald Acuna Jr. rode a torrid 20-game stretch into the middle contest Saturday of an interleague series against the Houston Astros, and he continued his stellar play. Acuna finished 2-for-3 with two walks and a seventh-inning grand slam that sent the Braves toward a 6-3 victory. Atlanta (91-64) has a magic number of one to clinch the National League East title for the seventh time in nine seasons heading into Sunday's series finale in Houston. Acuna was batting .363 with six homers and 16 RBIs over the previous 20 games, a stretch that started after he sat and watched the finale of a three-game series against the Los Angeles Dodgers on Aug. 27. Since then, he has more closely resembled the two-way threat who terrorized the NL before two separate season-ending knee injuries altered his stardom. "And it's understandable, right?" Braves manager Walt Weiss said of Acuna methodically rounding into his superstar form. "When you have both knees reconstructed, it takes time to, not only physically, but mentally have the confidence in really letting it fly. "I think we're seeing that now with Ronald again." Left-hander Martin Perez (9-9, 3.07 ERA) will start the series finale for the Braves. Perez earned his first win in six starts -- and the 100th victory of his career -- in the Braves' 6-3 triumph over the Chicago Cubs on Tuesday, allowing three runs (two earned) on five hits and four walks with two strikeouts over six innings. Perez was 0-3 with a 3.55 ERA in the five starts between wins, and he is 10-8 with a 3.72 ERA in 22 career appearances (21 starts) against the Astros. Right-hander Hunter Brown (6-3, 3.43 ERA) is scheduled to start for the Astros (77-78) as they attempt to avert a three-game series sweep on Sunday. Houston trails the Texas Rangers by one game atop the American League West and is two games behind the Chicago White Sox in the race for the AL's final wild-card spot. Brown matched his season high with 10 strikeouts against the Kansas City Royals on Tuesday, allowing one run on two hits and three walks over five innings in a 4-2 win. He is 3-0 with a 2.86 ERA over his last five starts. Brown is 1-1 with a 4.15 ERA across three career starts against the Braves. He recorded a 6-2 win over them on Sept. 13, 2025, allowing two runs on four hits and one walk with two strikeouts over 6 2/3 innings. Left-hander Steven Okert, Houston's second-most consistent reliever behind closer Josh Hader, has spent the last two weeks on the injured list with a hamstring strain. His absence continues to be felt, as the Astros have struggled with high-leverage situations. Right-hander reliever AJ Blubaugh allowed three runs on two hits and one walk while recording just one out in the seventh inning on Saturday. In seven appearances since Okert went on the IL, Blubaugh has surrendered nine runs on nine hits and five walks over six innings. Right-hander reliever Bryan Abreu allowed a walk-off home run to the Rays' Junior Caminero on Sept. 11 and surrendered the grand slam to Acuna that flipped the game on Saturday. Previously reliable relievers Blubaugh and Abreu -- in tandem with Okert -- have labored lately. "Those are our guys, and I trust them," Astros manager Joe Espada said. "And I'm going to continue to give them the ball." --Field Level Media

item.title: Iran and US trade threats after Houthi attacks escalate regional conflict
item.description: Iran said it had information such a move was being prepared, adding to the anxiety in a region already on edge after drone and missile strikes on Saudi Arabia.
item.dc:creator: Jana Choukeir, Doina Chiacu
item.content:encoded: Iran and the United States exchanged new threats on Sunday, with President Donald Trump warning Iran would fail economically or face its leadership being wiped out if it didn't make a deal, and the Iranian military saying it would retaliate harshly to any fresh attack. The conflict has looked stalemated for months, with no sign either side was ready for concessions even as it has deepened a global energy crisis, cratered swathes of Iran's economy and spilled over into new regional escalations. In a phone call with a Fox News reporter, Trump said Iran's leaders should make a deal, rot economically or be wiped out, the reporter said. However, with Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian expected in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly, Trump said he would be open to meeting him, the Fox reporter added. Trump has repeatedly made vague threats of major military escalations during the conflict that began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28, without carrying them out. Earlier, Iran's military central command said any new attack would trigger sustained retaliation against US bases and interests and that Washington's regional allies would be considered parties to the conflict. The Iranian military added that it had information that an attack was being prepared, without elaborating on what that information might be. HOUTHIS TARGET RIYADH US Gulf allies have already been badly scarred by a war that the US and Israel launched with no warning, bringing their cities under Iranian fire and hammering their economies with the crucial Strait of Hormuz waterway blockaded. On Saturday their predicament worsened further, with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi group launching [USN:L1N45B003 TEXT:"missile and drone strikes"] at the Saudi capital after having made sudden military gains in Yemen's reignited civil war earlier this month. Reuters video showed a massive plume of black smoke billowing from the area of Riyadh's main international airport following booms overnight. The US State Department issued a security alert citing the Houthi hostilities. It said there was potential for unforeseen escalation in the Middle East, and Americans should exercise more vigilance and be aware of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures. Saudi Arabia did not comment on the incident, though a Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had foiled other attacks on the kingdom. Recent escalation by the Houthis has forced Riyadh into a painful dilemma: continue airstrikes on the group to stop it seizing more Yemeni territory or step back in the hopes of averting drone strikes on critical infrastructure. ENERGY EXPORTS BLOCKADED The Houthi gains along the coast mean the group's forces now sit on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, giving them easier control over shipping travelling between the Red Sea and Asia and the ability to blockade the crucial waterway. With Iran already having blockaded most shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the oil-rich Gulf's energy exports are now almost entirely cut off from global markets, adding to pressure on oil prices. A US blockade of Iranian ports is meanwhile stopping Iran from selling its own oil, contributing to [USN:L1N44W081 TEXT:"major problems"] in the Islamic Republic's economy. Despite the economic damage, there is little sign of a return to the interim ceasefire agreement that was struck in June but [USN:L6N43F0R2 TEXT:"fell apart"] in July amid disputes over its terms. Iran reiterated on Sunday that it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the terms of that June agreement, as it interpreted them, were met. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said Iran would have to keep on fighting as well as negotiating, to push back its enemies and to consolidate any gains with diplomacy.

item.title: Un Israélien et un Palestinien abattus en Cisjordanie occupée
item.description: Un Israélien a été abattu dimanche en Cisjordanie occupée par un tireur palestinien présumé, a rapporté la police, tandis que des soldats israéliens ont tué un automobiliste palestinien qui, selon l'armée, tentait de les renverser.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Un Israélien a été abattu dimanche en Cisjordanie occupée par un tireur palestinien présumé, a rapporté la police, tandis que des soldats israéliens ont tué un automobiliste palestinien qui, selon l'armée, tentait de les renverser. Selon l'armée et la police israéliennes, le tireur a ouvert le feu depuis son véhicule sur des Israéliens rassemblés à proximité de la colonie de Neve Tzuf, près de Ramallah. Un homme grièvement blessé par balle a été déclaré mort à l'hôpital, a déclaré la police. Le tireur a été localisé quelques heures plus tard dans un hôpital de Ramallah et arrêté, a-t-elle ajouté. Peu après la fusillade, l'armée a annoncé avoir "éliminé" un automobiliste palestinien qui avait tenté de lancer sa voiture sur des soldats près de la colonie de Ganim, plus au nord en Cisjordanie. Aucun soldat n'a été blessé, a-t-elle ajouté.

item.title: El hermano de Diana compara trato que medios dan a Enrique y Meghan con el que sufrió la princesa
item.description: El trato que los medios de comunicación han dispensado al príncipe Enrique y a su esposa Meghan es comparable al que sufrió su madre, Diana, dijo el hermano de la difunta princesa en una entrevista publicada el domingo, en la que advirtió de que era necesario aprender de aquella época.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El trato que los medios de comunicación han dispensado al príncipe Enrique y a su esposa Meghan es comparable al que sufrió su madre, Diana, dijo el hermano de la difunta princesa en una entrevista publicada el domingo, en la que advirtió de que era necesario aprender de aquella época. Diana falleció a los 36 años en un accidente de tráfico en París en 1997, mientras unos fotógrafos la perseguían en moto, lo que desencadenó una oleada de dolor y un debate sobre si los medios de comunicación tenían alguna responsabilidad en su muerte. "Si te fijas en una noticia de un tabloide sobre Diana o sobre la pareja que mencionabas, Enrique y Meghan, ya sabes, pueden ser realmente, realmente desagradables", dijo a la BBC el hermano de Diana, el conde Charles Spencer. "Y creo que la gente debería aprender del ejemplo de Diana". "No estoy aquí para hablar en nombre de Enrique y Meghan, pero para cualquiera que esté siendo destrozado de esta manera a diario, debe de ser una influencia cancerosa en su vida", dijo. Enrique, el hijo menor de Diana, y Meghan, mencionaron el impacto de lo que ellos denominaban "medios tóxicos" tenía en sus vidas antes de renunciar a sus obligaciones reales y mudarse a Estados Unidos en 2020. También demandaron a gran parte de la prensa sensacionalista británica —con diversos grados de éxito— antes de regresar a Gran Bretaña en agosto. Spencer ha acaparado los titulares de todo el mundo durante la última semana después de que su libro, «Swan Song: Diana, My Sister», se publicara por entregas en el Daily Mail, en el que acusaba a su exmarido, el ahora rey Carlos, de mostrarse «eufórico» en las horas posteriores a su muerte. El palacio respondió afirmando que el rey «es consciente de que el dolor de la pérdida de un hermano puede nublar la razón, afectar al juicio y sesgar los recuerdos de formas que los demás no perciben, incluso muchos años después de dicha pérdida». La publicación del libro y el regreso de Harry y Meghan a Gran Bretaña suponen otro reto para el rey, que sigue sometiéndose a tratamiento contra el cáncer. La familia de Diana acusó a la familia real de mostrar una falta de apoyo o de atención hacia la difunta princesa antes de su muerte, una acusación que repitió Harry, quien actualmente se encuentra en gran medida distanciado del resto de la familia real.

item.title: Resurgent Acosta beats Martin for maiden MotoGP win in Austria
item.description: Pedro Acosta claimed the first MotoGP victory of his career in the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday, bouncing back from his sprint-race crash to beat world championship leader Jorge Martin at KTM's home Red Bull Ring circuit.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pedro Acosta claimed the first MotoGP victory of his career in the Austrian Grand Prix on Sunday, bouncing back from his [USN:L1N45B02X TEXT:"sprint-race"] crash to beat world championship leader Jorge Martin at KTM's home Red Bull Ring circuit. The 22-year-old Spaniard, who qualified third before crashing out while leading Saturday's sprint, seized the lead from [USN:L4N45B027 TEXT:"polesitter Martin"] on lap nine of the 28-lap race and never looked back. Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi completed the podium, while Trackhouse rider Ai Ogura finished fourth. It was an emotional moment for Acosta, nicknamed 'The Shark', who arrived in MotoGP with huge expectations after winning the Moto3 world title in 2021 and the Moto2 crown in 2023. "The first one is always special," Acosta said. "Nice way to close a season like this with KTM in front of all Austrian fans. Super happy for them because they deserve it even more than me." Acosta is set to leave KTM at the end of 2026 to join the factory Ducati team. Martin, the 2024 MotoGP champion, got off to a brilliant start but was overtaken by teammate Bezzecchi for the lead at Turn One on lap two. The 28-year-old responded immediately, reclaiming top spot at Turn Three on the same lap. However, Acosta's pace proved decisive and he passed Martin for the lead on lap nine before pulling away. "I want to congratulate Pedro. He fought a lot during the last few years to get this victory. This feeling is amazing for him, so I'm really happy for him," Martin said of his fellow Spaniard. "For myself, I think I did a great race. I was trying to manage the fuel. Then Pedro took me but I thought everything was under control. But step by step, he was stepping away. I tried to push a bit more but my rear tyre was completely destroyed. I did my best. "This is what we have to do every weekend for the rest of the season, and the fight is on. So I am really looking forward to continuing like this." Martin now has 306 points in the standings, a 12-point lead over compatriot and reigning MotoGP champion Marc Marquez ahead of next month's Japanese Grand Prix. Italian Bezzecchi is third with 264 points. Marquez endured a frustrating weekend as Ducati lacked the outright pace of the Aprilias. The seven-time MotoGP champion qualified second but slipped back on the opening lap and eventually finished fifth.

item.title: Cubs eye potential playoff berth in finale vs. Reds
item.description: The Chicago Cubs could not ask for a better gift than a healthy Dansby Swanson for the playoffs.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Chicago Cubs could not ask for a better gift than a healthy Dansby Swanson for the playoffs. Swanson came off the injured list on Friday after being sidelined for a month with a left oblique strain. On Saturday, he hit his 19th home run of the season to help the visiting Cubs record a 5-2 victory over the Cincinnati Reds. Chicago (86-69) can clinch a playoff spot with a win on Sunday afternoon against the Reds and a loss by the Arizona Diamondbacks to the New York Yankees. The Cubs are tied with the San Diego Padres (86-69) in the race for the top wild-card spot in the National League, one game ahead of the Philadelphia Phillies (85-70) and five games ahead of Arizona (81-74). "This is like uncharted territory for me," Swanson said. "I'm just grateful for all the support from the team. Today was just a complete effort from everyone. I love when (reliever Daniel) Palencia is out there and believes no one can hit him. That is when he is best." Palencia retired all six batters he faced in two innings on Saturday, striking out three. "His two innings were his best outing of the year," Cubs manager Craig Counsell said of Palencia. "Through this last week, we have to find out about our bullpen, and this was a good step in that direction." The bullpen took over for Matthew Boyd, who allowed two runs on two hits in five innings to pick up his first win since Aug. 9. Four relievers allowed only two hits the rest of the way. "If we want to be a team that plays for a long time, we need to get outs from the bullpen," Counsell said. "We have to figure out who is going to get it done." The Cubs are expected to send left-hander David Peterson (8-8, 5.11 ERA) to the mound on Sunday. He is coming off a solid start in which he allowed one earned run on three hits in six innings of a 7-3 victory over the Atlanta Braves on Monday. The 31-year-old is 1-2 with a 5.84 ERA in eight career appearances (seven starts) vs. Cincinnati (72-83), which has been eliminated from playoff contention and will counter with right-hander Rhett Lowder (6-11, 5.79 ERA) on Sunday. Lowder's last win came on Aug. 28, a 10-8 decision over the Cubs. He yielded three runs on six hits in five innings to improve to 1-1 with a 3.60 ERA in four career meetings (three starts) vs. Chicago. The 24-year-old is coming off a 4-0 loss to the Dodgers on Tuesday in a game in which he gave up three runs and five hits in five innings. The Reds rallied to forge a 2-2 tie on Saturday with two runs in the fifth inning before the game slipped away. "The only thing I would say is I'm jealous," Cincinnati manager Terry Francona said. "Me and Nap (bench coach Mike Napoli) were talking (Friday) night. We were looking at the scoreboard, like, man, that feeling of anxiety. I kind of miss that." --Field Level Media

item.title: USA Trump transforme son projet d'arc de triomphe en "complexe militaire"
item.description: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré dimanche avoir accepté, à la demande de l'armée, de convertir son projet d'arc de triomphe à Washington en complexe militaire chargé d'abriter et déployer drones et munitions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Le président américain Donald Trump a déclaré dimanche avoir accepté, à la demande de l'armée, de convertir son projet d'arc de triomphe à Washington en complexe militaire chargé d'abriter et déployer drones et munitions. Le président américain a mentionné des préoccupations de sécurité nationale à l'appui de cette décision, sans mentionner de menaces spécifiques. Donald Trump a déjà modifié son projet de salle de bal à la Maison blanche, contesté devant la justice, et le présente désormais comme un complexe militaire intégré nécessaire à la sécurité nationale. L'autorité américaine de l'aviation civile a estimé vendredi que le projet d'un arc de triomphe d'une hauteur de 76 mètres près du cimetière national d'Arlington ne présentait pas de risque pour l'aviation civile à condition qu'il soit surmonté en permanence de spots éclairants. Des experts en aéronautique avaient émis des inquiétudes quant au choix du site, non loin de l'aéroport Ronald-Reagan. Des anciens combattants ont également déposé un recours contre le projet en estimant qu'il abîmerait la perspective entre le Lincoln Memorial et le cimetière d'Arlington. Depuis le début de son second mandat en janvier 2025, Donald Trump a entrepris de remodeler en profondeur la capitale fédérale avec la volonté d'y laisser son empreinte. Outre la destruction de l'aile Est de la Maison blanche pour y construire sa salle de bal, le président américain a fait rénover le bassin réfléchissant du Lincoln Memorial, désormais recouvert d'algues, et menace de démolir le Kennedy Center, haut lieu culturel de la ville, depuis que la justice lui a refusé d'y accoler son nom.

item.title: Macron y Carney se reunirán en un archipiélago francés del Atlántico, en un gesto dirigido a Trump
item.description: El presidente Emmanuel Macron llegó el domingo al territorio francés de San Pedro y Miquelón para mantener conversaciones con el primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, semanas después de que el presidente Donald Trump publicó una imagen en la que se veía a las islas cubiertas por la bandera estadounidense.
item.dc:creator: John Irish
item.content:encoded: El presidente Emmanuel Macron llegó el domingo al territorio francés de San Pedro y Miquelón para mantener conversaciones con el primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney, semanas después de que el presidente Donald Trump publicó una imagen en la que se veía a las islas cubiertas por la bandera estadounidense. La visita de Macron al archipiélago situado frente a la costa atlántica de Canadá es la primera que realiza un presidente francés desde 2014 y coincide con un acercamiento de Canadá a la Unión Europea en un contexto de una guerra comercial cada vez más encarnizada con Estados Unidos. San Pedro y Miquelón es el único territorio que le queda a Francia en Norteamérica, y las autoridades francesas dijeron que el viaje de Macron subrayaría la soberanía francesa y pondría de relieve los estrechos vínculos con Canadá. "No hay duda (de que es francés)", dijo Macron tras aterrizar el sábado por la noche en este territorio de 5.800 habitantes. "No vamos a afirmarlo todos los días porque la gente tenga ideas extrañas o diga cosas raras", dijo a periodistas en respuesta a una pregunta sobre el mapa de Trump. LA VISITA TIENE UN PESO SIMBÓLICO Los diplomáticos señalaron que la visita de Macron, que se dirigía a la Asamblea General anual de las Naciones Unidas en la que se reúnen los líderes mundiales, tenía un peso simbólico tras la publicación de Trump en las redes sociales. La imagen que compartió Trump mostraba la bandera de Estados Unidos extendida sobre Estados Unidos, Canadá, Groenlandia, Islandia, México, Centroamérica y el Caribe, y llevaba la leyenda "Estados Unidos de América". Incluía San Pedro y Miquelón y los territorios franceses del Caribe. Francia no respondió públicamente a la publicación en ese momento. Para Francia, San Pedro y Miquelón reviste una importancia estratégica debido a su ubicación a las puertas de Estados Unidos y del Ártico, explicó un responsable de la Presidencia francesa a los periodistas en una rueda de prensa previa a la visita. El territorio también ocupa un lugar clave en la cooperación de Francia con Canadá, entre otros ámbitos, en materia de energía, uno de los temas centrales de la reunión del domingo entre Macron y Carney.

item.title: White Sox continue push toward playoffs in finale against Tigers
item.description: Heading into the finale of a four-game set against the Detroit Tigers on Sunday afternoon, the host Chicago White Sox are desperate for a hero.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Heading into the finale of a four-game set against the Detroit Tigers on Sunday afternoon, the host Chicago White Sox are desperate for a hero. Miguel Vargas wants to fill that spot. The All-Star slugged his 33rd home run of the season on Saturday to help Chicago (79-76) beat Detroit 3-1 and stay a game behind the Cleveland Guardians atop the American League Central. The White Sox hold a two-game lead over the Houston Astros in the race for the third and final AL wild-card berth. "That's what I work for. That's why I wake up every day and work so hard for these types of moments," Vargas said. "And for me, this group has been pushing me every single day. I've never been thinking about my individual stats. I just want to go out there and do the best for my team and have some fun and always try hard." Davis Martin (9-7, 3.96 ERA) will make his fourth appearance since being activated from the 15-day injured list (finger blister). The right-hander has a 1.13 ERA in three outings since his return, giving up just three runs (two earned), but he has only an 0-1 record to show for it. Martin threw 5 1/3 innings of one-run, two-hit ball against Cleveland on Tuesday in a no-decision. He entered after Chris Murphy gave up three runs in two-thirds of an inning as the opener in Chicago's 7-6 loss. Martin is 1-2 with a 3.49 ERA in seven career games (six starts) against the Tigers. The 29-year-old surrendered just one run on five hits across six innings in Detroit on June 21, striking out four and walking three in a no-decision. Chicago lost 5-4 in 10 innings. On June 10, Martin had a 9-2 record and a 2.41 ERA after a 2-1 win over the Atlanta Braves. He has not won since, piling up five losses and nine no-decisions. Meanwhile, Detroit (73-82) is nearing the mathematical end to a disappointing season. After consecutive playoff appearances, the Tigers will be eliminated from postseason contention with their next loss. Detroit left 11 runners on base in the club's third loss in four games on Saturday. "It feels good to have opportunities. It doesn't feel good when you miss out on them," Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said. "It's tough when you leave that many on, but you don't want to not have them on there and not have the chance." As he makes his 20th start of the season for Detroit on Sunday, right-hander Troy Melton (8-4, 2.52 ERA) is looking to improve on what has been a forgettable September. After posting a 2.10 ERA in August, the 25-year-old has allowed 11 earned runs in 13 2/3 innings across his past three starts. On Monday, Melton lasted just 2 2/3 innings against the Toronto Blue Jays. He gave up two runs on five hits while walking four and striking out three in a no-decision. He needed 76 pitches to record eight outs in a game the Tigers won 6-5. In five career appearances (four starts) against the White Sox, Melton is 2-0 with a 1.48 ERA. He has faced them three times this year, going 1-0 with a 1.56 ERA, allowing three earned runs in 17 1/3 innings. The Tigers are 1-2 in his starts against the White Sox. --Field Level Media

item.title: Ucrania lanza el mayor ataque con drones contra Moscú, durante las elecciones en Rusia
item.description: Ucrania lanzó el domingo lo que el alcalde de Moscú calificó como el mayor ataque con drones hasta la fecha contra la capital rusa, mientras los rusos votaban en la última jornada de unas elecciones parlamentarias que el presidente Vladimir Putin ha presentado como una prueba del apoyo a la guerra.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Osborn, Vladimir Soldatkin
item.content:encoded: Ucrania lanzó el domingo lo que el alcalde de Moscú calificó como el mayor ataque con drones hasta la fecha contra la capital rusa, mientras los rusos votaban en la última jornada de unas elecciones parlamentarias que el presidente Vladimir Putin ha presentado como una prueba del apoyo a la guerra. Los ataques con drones causaron la muerte de dos personas en la región de Moscú temprano, y una tercera murió en un hospital, dijo el gobernador de la region, Andrei Vorobyov. Otras dos murieron en la parte de la región ucraniana de Jersón controlada por Rusia, entre ellas un funcionario electoral, según el alcalde de Moscú, Serguéi Sobianin, y las autoridades electorales. Ademas, resultó dañada una instalación de la refinería de petróleo de Moscú, que ya había sido objeto de bombardeos. "Se ha repelido el mayor ataque de drones enemigos", dijo Sobianin en Telegram. "Este ataque sin precedentes fue claramente planeado con el objetivo de perturbar las elecciones. El enemigo no lo ha conseguido". En las elecciones a la Duma Estatal, las primeras desde que Rusia inició su guerra a gran escala en Ucrania en febrero de 2022, se espera que el partido gobernante, Rusia Unida, conserve fácilmente su dominio en un sistema político que, según los críticos, no tolera la disidencia. Es probable que el Kremlin presente el resultado como prueba del respaldo público a las políticas de Putin y a la guerra, que ya entra en su quinto año sin que haya indicios de que vaya a terminar pronto. Las autoridades electorales han dicho que los tres días de votaciones se han desarrollado sin incidentes, a pesar de los ciberataques. A última hora de la mañana del domingo, la participación superaba el 45% tanto en las elecciones a la Duma como en las regionales, informó la presidenta de la Comisión Electoral Central, Ella Pamfilova. A la mayoría de los candidatos contrarios a la guerra se les ha prohibido presentarse a las elecciones. Los que sí se presentaron, pertenecientes al partido liberal Yabloko, dijeron que temían por su libertad, después de que los tribunales condenaron a largas penas de cárcel a dos figuras destacadas del partido antes de las elecciones por sus comentarios sobre el conflicto. Desacreditar al ejército o difundir lo que las autoridades consideran "noticias falsas" se castiga con largas penas de prisión. En un pequeño acto de rebeldía, el líder de Yabloko, Nikolai Rybakov, anuló de forma ostensible su papeleta, escribiendo el nombre de su partido y el lema "Por la paz". El Kremlin dice que la unidad nacional y cierta censura son necesarias durante lo que denomina su "operación militar especial" en Ucrania, que presenta el conflicto —el más mortífero de Europa desde la Segunda Guerra Mundial— como parte de una lucha existencial contra un Occidente hostil.

item.title: Luxembourg deploys additional detection assets following drone sightings
item.description: Luxembourg's government said on Sunday that additional detection assets have been deployed to strengthen airspace monitoring, after Luxembourg Airport temporarily suspended services late on Friday due to the sighting of drones.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Luxembourg's government said on Sunday that additional detection assets have been deployed to strengthen airspace monitoring, after Luxembourg Airport temporarily suspended services late on Friday due to the sighting of drones. "To strengthen airspace monitoring and analysis capabilities, additional detection assets have been deployed, including resources provided by foreign partners," the government said in a statement. "These supplementary systems have contributed to further consolidating airspace surveillance and contributed to a better assessment of the situation by the competent authorities," it added. The government also said that on Saturday evening police "received several reports concerning the suspected presence of drones within national airspace" but that "following verifications, no situation required an operational intervention by the authorities". Luxembourg's authorities launched an investigation after flight operations had been temporarily suspended on Friday evening following the visual sighting of "unidentified and unauthorized drones". Prime Minister Luc Frieden told reporters on Saturday that his country had been "confronted with something new for Luxembourg, the presence of potentially bigger drones in the Luxembourg airspace". "We have observed this over the past few days, which led to the precautionary measure last night," he said. On Sunday, Luxembourg's government said its drone assessment cell is continuing work with partners to ensure monitoring of the situation.

item.title: Italy to ban veils in schools, limit foreign students per class, Meloni says
item.description: Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni played up her right-wing credentials at a youth event organized by her party.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italy is preparing to ban face coverings in schools and to cap the number of foreign students per class, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said on Sunday as she played up her right-wing credentials at a youth event organised by her party. Italy is among the European countries most exposed to migrant arrivals because of its central Mediterranean location, making migration a hot-button issue and a major challenge for successive governments. The integration of migrants, particularly those from Muslim-majority countries, remains contentious in Italian politics and society. Debates over religious symbols, cultural integration, citizenship rules and immigration policy frequently polarize public opinion. "A measure will soon be presented to a Cabinet meeting to legally establish a maximum number of foreign students per class. It also requires parents of foreign students facing serious difficulties integrating into the school system to learn Italian and bans burqas and niqabs in schools," Meloni told an annual gathering of the youth wing of her Brothers of Italy party. "If there is only one child in a class who doesn't understand Italian, that child will likely be able to learn the language and integrate quickly with the help of classmates and teachers. However, if the number of children who don't understand the language becomes large - or even the majority - that is no longer integration; it is neglect," she added. Meloni did not specify what the maximum number of foreign students per class would be. Students who are not Italian citizens account for 11.6% of those enrolled in Italian schools — nearly 12 in every 100 students — according to Fondazione ISMU, a research institution. "You must go to school with your face uncovered, and in Italy no one, in the name of a real or supposed tradition, can decide that a young woman must hide herself, " Meloni said.

item.title: Iran seals French language centre in Tehran, accuses it of illegal activities
item.description: Iranian authorities have sealed a French language centre affiliated with the French embassy in Tehran following a judicial order, the Tehran prosecutor's office said on Sunday according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iranian authorities have sealed a French language centre affiliated with the French embassy in Tehran following a judicial order, the Tehran prosecutor's office said on Sunday according to the semi-official Tasnim news agency. The centre operated for years under the cover of foreign-language teaching despite repeated warnings to obtain a licence, authorities said, accusing it of activities against Iranian culture and national security, including identifying and building networks as well as facilitating the departure of skilled Iranians from the country.

item.title: ウクライナがモスクワ攻撃、ロシア下院選最終日 与党が多数派維持へ
item.description:
Andrew Osborn Vladimir Soldatkin
［モスクワ ２０日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Andrew Osborn　Vladimir Soldatkin

［モスクワ　２０日　ロイター］ - ロシアの首都モスクワのソビャニン市長は２０日、ウクライナによる過去最大規模のドローン（無人機）攻撃を撃退したと述べた。２０日はロシア下院選の投票最終日に当たる。

ソビャニン氏は通信アプリ「テレグラム」で「敵のドローンによる過去最大の攻撃を撃退した」とし、「この前例のない攻撃は明らかに選挙の妨害を目的に計画されたものだ。敵の試みは失敗した」と述べた。

同氏と選挙管理当局によると、ドローン攻撃によりモスクワ州で２人死亡。過去に標的となったモスクワの製油所施設も被害を受けた。またロシアが実効支配するウクライナ南部ヘルソン州で選挙管理委員を含む２人が死亡した。

＜下院選、与党が多数派維持へ＞

ロシアが２０２２年２月にウクライナへの本格侵攻を開始して以降で初となる今回の下院選は、反戦を掲げる候補者の大半の立候補が禁じられ、与党「統一ロシア」が難なく多数派を維持するとみられている。

選挙管理当局によると、１９日にサイバー攻撃が報告されたものの、３日間の投票はおおむね順調に進んだ。インタファクス通信が中央選挙管理委員会の情報として伝えたところによると、モスクワ時間の２０日午後早い段階で投票率は５０％を超えた。

暫定結果は２０日１８００ＧＭＴ（日本時間２１日午前３時）ごろに発表され、より詳細な結果は２１日に発表される見通し。

item.title: Palestinian gunman shoots dead Israeli in the West Bank, soldiers kill motorist
item.description: It was not clear whether the incidents on the eve of Yom Kippur were connected.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Violence flared in the occupied West Bank on Sunday when a suspected Palestinian gunman shot dead an Israeli man, police said, and Israeli soldiers killed a Palestinian motorist who the military said was attempting to run them over. The gunman opened fire from his vehicle at Israelis gathered at a spring near the settlement of Neve Tzuf, near Ramallah, according to the Israeli military and police. Medics who arrived at the scene of the shooting said they found a man in a car suffering from critical gunshot wounds. He was pronounced dead at hospital, police said. The gunman was located a few hours later at a hospital in Ramallah and arrested, police said. Shortly after the shooting, the military said that its forces "eliminated" a Palestinian driver who had attempted a ramming attack on soldiers near the settlement of Ganim, further north in the West Bank. No soldiers were hurt, it said. Reuters was not able to immediately verify the soldiers' account. It was not clear whether the fatal incidents, on the eve of the Jewish holy day of Yom Kippur, were connected. Following the incidents, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he had instructed security agencies to beef up their forces and carry out arrests and offensive activities in the area. Palestinian militant group Hamas praised the shooting attack but did not claim responsibility for it. Violence has escalated in the West Bank since Hamas' October 7, 2023, attack on Israel and the ensuing Israeli military offensive in Gaza . The West Bank violence has included a sharp rise in attacks by [USN:L6N44Y077 TEXT:"militant settlers"] on Palestinians, as well as sweeping Israeli military raids and Palestinian attacks on Israelis.

item.title: Trump to use Washington arch as military complex for drones and snipers
item.description: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday the triumphal arch he plans to build near Arlington National Cemetery in Washington would double as a "military complex" housing drones and snipers, as well as storing large quantities of ammunition.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Layne, Anusha Devang Shah
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump said on Sunday the triumphal arch he plans to build near Arlington National Cemetery in Washington would double as a "military complex" housing drones and snipers, as well as storing large quantities of ammunition. The president cited national security concerns for the move, echoing the rationale offered for the roughly $400 million [USN:S0N42U038 TEXT:"ballroom complex"] being built on the site of the White House's former East Wing. He did not identify any specific threats. The projects are part of Trump's ambitious effort to [USN:L6N41H110 TEXT:"reshape Washington"], including a push to add his name to the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The plans have drawn criticism from preservationists and others who argue they could alter or diminish historic landmarks. In a social media post, Trump said that at the "strong request" of the military he had agreed to turn the 250-foot (76-meter) arch "into a top grade Military Complex/Triumphal Arch, to house, store, and have the rapid ability to use large numbers of drones, plus Snipers, on both the roof and plaza areas, and additionally have and hold large quantities of sniper ammunition in storage." A US military official told Reuters that the Defense Department had nothing to add beyond Trump's social media post. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Trump did not elaborate on why such capabilities would be needed at the arch. His proposed White House ballroom has already been touted as a [USN:L1N41W12V TEXT:"drone facility"] to protect Washington. EXPERT QUESTIONS MILITARY RATIONALE Mark Cancian, a retired Marine colonel, said the move appeared aimed at countering opposition to the arch, which is planned for a traffic circle near Arlington National Cemetery, about a mile from Fort Myer, an active Army installation, and roughly 2 miles (3.2 km) from the Pentagon. "It looks like it's tacked on in order to strengthen the rationale for construction," Cancian, a senior adviser with the Defense and Security Department at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, a Washington-based think tank, told Reuters. "There is this military facility (Fort Myer) long established with a variety of military capabilities one mile away. So why you need this one isn't clear." Cancian also said that storing ammunition at the arch would create logistical challenges and questioned the value of positioning snipers there. LEGAL CHALLENGES MOUNT US District Judge Tanya Chutkan earlier this month ordered the Trump administration to [USN:L1N44W0QM TEXT:"give 48 hours' notice"] before engaging in any activity on the site of the triumphal arch. Her ruling came a day after the US Interior Department announced plans to move forward soon with work on the arch despite legal challenges and the lack of final approval from a government planning authority. The Federal Aviation Administration said last week that the arch would [USN:L1N45A0PQ TEXT:"not pose a hazard"] to aircraft but would be required to have an "eternal flame" on top, clearing an aviation hurdle for the arch, which Trump proposed to mark the nation's 250th anniversary. Aviation experts have raised safety concerns given its proximity to Reagan Washington National Airport while veterans have sued to block the arch, arguing it would destroy the historic sightline between the Lincoln Memorial and Arlington National Cemetery.

item.title: Pirates' Brandon Lowe takes HR barrage into finale vs. Royals
item.description: The Pittsburgh Pirates will look to complete a three-game sweep of the visiting Kansas City Royals on Sunday afternoon behind Brandon Lowe, who has homered in four of his last five games.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Pittsburgh Pirates will look to complete a three-game sweep of the visiting Kansas City Royals on Sunday afternoon behind Brandon Lowe, who has homered in four of his last five games. Lowe's two-run homer in the eighth inning on Saturday lifted Pittsburgh (78-77) to a 6-5 victory over Kansas City (67-88). The win was the Pirates' 13th in their last 19 games. Lowe's 33rd homer was the 96th hit by the club at home this season, breaking a franchise mark established in 1947. It also was Lowe's 19th homer at home, eclipsing Brian Giles' club mark, set in 2001. "The best part of it is coming out with a win," Lowe said. "Records are cool, but a win is a whole lot better."
